newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firm, trade quiet ahead of KPC talks.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firm, trade quiet ahead of KPC talks.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices edged higher on Friday due to firmer crudes, traders said.
Activity remained quiet in the wet market as petrochemical end-users kept a low profile prior to term talks with Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC), they said.
"End-users don"t want to give KPC an impression that the market is bullish ahead of the talks," one trader said.
Naphtha"s near-term spreads narrowed slightly as buyers held back amid steep backwardation, traders said.
The one-month spread from first-half April was indicated at about plus $8.00/10.00, compared with Thursday"s $9.00/10.00.

Open-spec naphtha for second-half April was quoted at $232.00/234.00 per tonne. On Thursday, it was sold once to a South Korean firm at $233.00, and again to a European trader at $232.00, traders said.
First-half April was assessed at $237.00/240.00, up from late Thursday"s $236.50/238.50.

KPC will hold term talks with about a dozen trading houses, oil firms and petrochemical end-users from Japan and South Korea from next Monday in Singapore for one-year supply contracts starting in March, traders said.
